candidates.statement: 6 In addition to the recommendations in this guidance, clinical testing sites should conduct the clinical portion of the study using good clinical practice to ensure participant safety and data integrity.
candidates.context: 5 When discussing the recommendations for achieving and maintaining data integrity, this guidance will generally reference BA and BE studies. As stated, the recommendations also apply to clinical pharmacologic studies supporting CDER-regulated BLAs. FDA expects that all data submitted to the Agency are accurate, complete, and reliable, and that 27 applicants and testing sites achieve and maintain data integrity throughout the data lifecycle of 28 the product(s) or biologic therapeutic(s) (see section II – Background). This guidance provides 29 recommendations to achieve and maintain data integrity with respect to (1) applicants, (2) testing 30 site management, and (3) implementation and management of a quality management system. 31

candidates.statement: For purposes of this guidance, data integrity refers to the accuracy, completeness, and reliability 59 of data. Accurate, complete, and reliable data should be attributable to the person generating the 60 data, legible, contemporaneously recorded, original or a true copy, and accurate (ALCOA). 8
candidates.context: Requirements for submitting BA and BE data in INDs, NDAs, ANDAs, and amendments and 49 supplements to these applications, the definitions of BA and BE, and the types of in vitro and in 50 vivo studies that are appropriate to measure BA and establish BE are set forth in 21 CFR parts 51 312, 314, and 320. Requirements for BLAs and amendments and supplements to these 52 applications are included in 21 CFR part 601. FDA expects that all data submitted to the 53 Agency, including data from BA and BE studies submitted in support of INDs, NDAs, and 54 ANDAs and clinical pharmacologic studies submitted in support of BLAs, is accurate, complete, 55 and reliable, and that industry maintain data integrity throughout the data lifecycle of the 56 product(s) or biologic therapeutic(s). 57 These characteristics of the data should be maintained throughout the data lifecycle. 62

candidates.statement: Applicants should ensure the integrity and confidentiality of data generated by and managed for 108 BA and BE studies and applicants should implement an appropriate system to manage data 109 quality throughout all stages of the BA and BE study. 12 The applicant’s quality management 110 system should include the design and implementation of efficient protocols including tools and 111 procedures for study conduct (including data collection and management) to support 112 participant’s rights, safety, and well-being and the reliability of study results. 13

candidates.statement: Applicants should develop and use a monitoring plan to ensure that testing sites are appropriately 154 assessing, controlling, communicating, and reviewing risks 14 to the quality and integrity of study 155 data and protecting participants enrolled in the study. The procedures and processes tailored to 156 monitor the critical aspects of the studies should be clearly delineated from and be independent 157 of the testing site’s quality assurance monitoring plans. As part of the monitoring plan, 158 applicants should conduct audits to verify testing sites’ compliance with the monitoring plan (see 159 section III.A.2.b of this guidance). 160
candidates.context: Applicants should understand and consider the entire data-flow in developing and using their 162 monitoring plan. candidates.statement: The extent of monitoring should be proportionate to the risk that the data may be compromised. 173 For example, the bioanalysis of participant samples from in vivo BA and BE studies is essential 174 to those studies providing pivotal data in support of approval of the drug product application. 175 FDA has increasingly found that the inability to verify and rely on the bioanalysis of participant 176 samples from those studies undermines the reliability of the clinical study data, jeopardizing 177 application approvability and making the risks that study participants were exposed to by 178 participating in the studies unjustifiable. Therefore, bioanalytical portions of the studies may 179 warrant closer oversight and monitoring by applicants to ensure that the performance of the 180 analytical methods used for in vivo BA and BE studies are in accordance with the applicable 181 FDA regulations and recommendations, based on its intended purpose. 182

candidates.statement: With a robust quality management system, testing site management should demonstrate strong 301 and visible support for the system and ensure its implementation throughout the organization, 302 which also goes toward encouraging a quality culture.
